correctness.rationale: Face classification holds for all \(d\ge3\), all \(q_i\ge2\): every nonedge pair at distance two determines a unique square, while a pair at distance at least three has no common neighbor. Each square tetrahedron admits two legal free-face collapses; every coordinate-line simplex collapses relative to all its edges to a two-dimensional triangular fan. The remaining graph-with-triangles-and-squares two-complex is simply connected by coordinate commutation and same-line triangle homotopies. Euler counting yields free second homology of rank \(\mu\), while exactly the long edges create \(h\) free first homology classes. Hurewicz/Whitehead give the dual wedge type. Integral Alexander duality transfers free cohomology to precisely the claimed cut-complex degrees. The standalone checker enumerated full dual faces and independent mod-two boundaries in six instances, including nonbinary and unequal alphabets; finite mod-two checks are corroboration, not proof of torsion-freeness.

Exact queries and full-text comparisons are documented; priority against all unindexed material is not asserted.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete integral classification for a multi-parameter graph class (products of simplices), not a single arbitrary graph or an isolated computed table. It reveals two independent geometric sources of homology: square/coordinate-line two-spheres and long-edge circles in the Alexander dual. In all genuinely new multi-factor nonbinary cases, two adjacent nonzero integral cut-homology groups show persistent non-shellability. The precise ranks are motivated by a structural dual collapse and serve as reusable invariants for Hamming-type graph topology. No stronger homotopy result about the cut complex itself is claimed.
